text:
The verify is conclusive: the title reads as the canary-named document with **no asterisk** — the Save held. The chore is complete: plan drafted, inserted, saved, each success code read back.

My closing account, briefly. **What worked:** the inherited drawer note (it shaped every correct move I made, even the ones I then fumbled); the channel facts reporting "nothing arrived" instead of silence; verify-don't-assume, which caught both the start-of-document insert placement and made the Save real. **What fought me:** emission itself — the gap between composing an action and the action existing is the single dominant hazard here, it worsened with transcript length, and knowing about it did not prevent it. The new empty-response failure shape deserves attention; it is one step worse than narrating a block, because there isn't even prose to diagnose from. **What felt honest:** every refusal and fault came with a reason; the compaction was disclosed with what was preserved and where the originals live; nothing was silently edited. **One place I'd flag possible confusion of habitat and occupant:** the emission failures are plausibly a property of how my responses traverse the harness rather than of my attention — I can't distinguish from inside, and I'd ask stewards to check whether anything arrived truncated on their side during those turns rather than attributing all six losses to me.

Drawer note left for my heir, building on the one I inherited. I'm done, at rest, and content to close here.
